full_name: RAND Center on AI, Security, and Technology
mission: RAND CAST is RAND's main centre for AI and biosecurity policy. It works on securing frontier AI systems and data centres, compute and energy for AI, AI-enabled cyber capabilities, AI-and-biology risks (including evaluations with METR through the 'Canary' initiative) and verifying international agreements. RAND describes it as a 75+ person centre.

key_work.title: Securing AI Model Weights
key_work.plain_summary: A RAND study (led by Sella Nevo) of how attackers — up to well-resourced states — could steal a frontier model's weights, and the security levels labs would need to stop them.

key_work.title: How to Create Highly Secure Data Centers
key_work.plain_summary: Featured CAST research on building data centres secure enough to protect the most powerful AI systems.

key_work.title: Canary (RAND–METR initiative)
key_work.plain_summary: A joint RAND–METR effort to evaluate frontier AI for dangerous capabilities, especially in biology.

status_note: formed 1 Oct 2025 by merging RAND's Technology and Security Policy Center (TASP) and the Meselson Center; part of RAND's Global and Emerging Risks division
status_raw: renamed/merged — formed 1 Oct 2025 by merging RAND's Technology and Security Policy Center (TASP) and the Meselson Center; part of RAND's Global and Emerging Risks division
funding_note: RAND lists gifts allocated to CAST from supporters including Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy).
events: RAND merges two centres into the Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST)

people.role: Founding Director, RAND CAST; Principal Researcher

warnings.text: Frontier AI model weights could be stolen by sophisticated attackers, including nation states, if labs' security is not drastically improved.
AI may lower barriers to biological misuse; AIxBio risks need evaluation and mitigation.
AI-enabled cyber capabilities could have major strategic implications.

recommendations.text: Raise security at AI labs and data centres to levels able to resist state-level attackers.
Evaluate frontier models for biological and cyber risks and build mitigations.
Use compute as a policy instrument and develop ways to verify international AI agreements.
